Terms starting with #.
Freedom of association and collective bargaining; no forced labour; no child labour; no discrimination at work.

children.topic: A civil wrong, not a crime

children.topic: A firm promise on set terms (offer)
children.note: An offer shows a willingness to be bound as soon as the other person accepts. It can be spoken, written or shown by conduct.

children.topic: A promise the law will enforce
children.note: A contract is an agreement between two or more people that creates rights and duties a court will back up. Not every promise is a contract.
It must be in writing, signed by the maker (testator), and witnessed by at least two people. The maker must be an adult of sound mind acting freely.
When a matatu driver kills someone by dangerous driving, the State prosecutes because everyone's safety is at stake, not just the victim's family.
A buyer who says they accept, acts like the owner, or keeps goods too long without complaint loses the right to reject, but can still claim damages.
Authority truly given, either in words (express) or understood from the job (implied).
An administrator takes over to rescue the company or get creditors a better result. A moratorium stops creditors suing meanwhile.
Admissible evidence is relevant and is not shut out by any rule, such as the hearsay rule or a privilege.

Obey instructions, use care and skill, act personally, avoid conflicts of interest, take no secret profit and account for money.

AI tools sometimes make up cases, quotes and citations that look real. These are called 'hallucinations'.
The main aim is to put the injured person back, as far as money can, where they would have been if the wrong had not happened.

children.topic: An invitation to bargain (invitation to treat)
children.note: Shop displays, price lists and most adverts only invite people to make offers. The customer makes the offer and the shop accepts at the till.

After twelve months of service, a worker is entitled to at least 21 working days of paid annual leave.
You may sue for yourself, for someone who cannot act, for a group, in the public interest, or as an association for members. This is wide standing (locus standi
The principal makes it look as if the agent has authority, the third party relies on it, and the principal is bound.
Would a fair-minded, informed observer see a real possibility of bias? (Porter v Magill, 2001).
Link the rule to the specific facts. Say why each fact helps or hurts each side. This is where most marks are won or lost.
Thomas Aquinas linked eternal law (God's plan), natural law (our reasoned share of it), divine law (revealed) and human law (made by rulers).

children.topic: Aquinas: unjust law is no law
children.note: An unjust law keeps only the outward look of law; it is a corruption of law (lex iniusta non est lex).
Article 159 tells courts to do justice without undue regard to procedural technicalities and to promote alternative and traditional dispute resolution. This ech

The Constitution told Parliament to set up a court with the status of the High Court for employment and labour disputes.
The High Court supervises lower courts and any body doing judicial or quasi-judicial work. It can call for their records and make orders to keep justice fair.
Kadhis' courts decide Muslim law questions of personal status, marriage, divorce and inheritance, but only where all parties are Muslim and agree to go there.
Any law, including customary law, that conflicts with the Constitution is invalid to that extent.
The general rules of international law form part of Kenyan law automatically.
Any treaty or convention Kenya has ratified becomes part of Kenyan law under the Constitution.
Treaties, custom, general principles of law, and (as helpers) court decisions and the writings of experts. Article 38 sets no ranking among them.

Every person has the right to fair labour practices.
Workers have rights to fair pay, reasonable working conditions, to form and join a trade union, and to go on strike.
The family is the basic unit of society. Adults may marry only with both people's free consent. Spouses have equal rights when they marry, during the marriage a
Consumers have rights to goods and services of reasonable quality, to information, to protection of health, safety and money, and to compensation for loss or in
Everyone has a right to administrative action that is quick, efficient, lawful, reasonable and fair in procedure. Kenya made good administration a constitutiona
If a decision has hurt, or may hurt, one of your rights, you can ask for the reasons in writing.
An arrested person must be told of the right to stay silent, and cannot be forced to confess or make an admission that could be used against them.

All land belongs to the people of Kenya collectively as a nation, as communities and as individuals. It is classified as public, community or private.

Land held by communities sharing ethnicity, culture or similar interest, such as grazing areas, shrines, ancestral lands and community forests. Unregistered com
Non-citizens may hold land only on leasehold, for at most 99 years. A longer grant is cut down to 99 years. A company counts as a citizen only if wholly owned b
The NLC manages public land for both levels of government, recommends land policy, investigates historical land injustices and encourages traditional dispute re
The company's internal rules on meetings, directors and shares. Model articles apply where the company has not written its own.
Making someone fear that force is about to be used on them, such as raising a fist at a tout. No touching is needed.
Intending a crime and going beyond mere preparation towards it, e.g. breaking a duka lock but being caught before taking anything.
Law is a command from a sovereign whom people habitually obey, backed by a sanction (threat of punishment).

The civil standard: is the claim more likely true than not? Lord Denning put it this way in Miller v Minister of Pensions.
Set the classic test for the mental capacity to make a will: understand the act, the property and the people with claims, with no delusion warping the choice.
Threats of violence need only be one reason for signing, not the main one, for the contract to be set aside.

Intentional, unwanted physical contact with another person, such as a slap or a shove off a matatu step.
The court must be sure of guilt. If a reasonable doubt remains, the accused must be acquitted.
The criminal standard. The court must be sure of guilt; a real, sensible doubt means acquittal.

A solicitor who used information from the trust to make a profit held it on constructive trust, though he acted honestly. He got an allowance for his work.
Companies borrow using debentures and give security. A fixed charge is over a specific asset; a floating charge hovers over changing assets like stock.
The prosecution must prove guilt; the accused need not prove innocence. Exceptions are narrow, e.g. insanity or where an Act says otherwise.
An agent acts without authority, and the principal later approves the act. The approval works backwards as if authority existed.
A spouse of a citizen married for at least seven years, a lawful resident of at least seven years (on conditions set by Parliament), or a child adopted by a cit
Terms starting with C.
A car owner paid by a bad cheque told the police and AA at once. This clear act cancelled the voidable deal before the car reached a later buyer.
An advert promising money to anyone who fell ill after using the smoke ball was a real offer to the world. The bank deposit showed it was serious, and using the
The settlor must really mean to create a trust, not just hope or wish. No special words are needed: in Paul v Constance a couple's casual words about a bank acc
An order cancelling an unlawful decision so it has no effect. England renamed it a "quashing order" in 2004; Kenyan courts still use the old name.
Criminal law: the state prosecutes a wrong against society and can punish (jail, fine). Civil law: one person sues another for a remedy such as money, e.g. a ma
A written deal on pay and terms negotiated between a union and employer. Once registered it binds both sides.

A competent witness can understand questions and give sensible answers. A court tests a young child's understanding first (voir dire).
Big, root terms. Breaking one lets the other side end the contract and claim damages.

After a waiting period the court confirms the grant and approves how the estate will be shared. Only then can land be transferred to heirs.
Any law, including customary law, that clashes with the Constitution is void to the extent of the clash. Any act or omission against it is invalid.
An agreement between two or more people to commit a crime. The agreement itself is the offence.
The supreme law. It binds every person and every state organ, nationally and in the counties, and its validity cannot be challenged in any court.

children.topic: Contract of service vs for services
children.note: An employee works under a contract of service. An independent contractor (like a fundi hired for one job) works under a contract for services.
Each spouse's share follows what they contributed. Money counts, and so does unpaid work: childcare, running the home, working the family farm.
The victim was partly to blame, for example by not wearing a seat belt. Damages are cut by the victim's share of fault rather than refused.
There are moral standards we can discover by reason, and human law should conform to them.
Regulates legal education: accredits and licenses law schools, sets core courses, and has run the Bar examination since the 2014 amendments.
Hears appeals from the High Court and from other courts or tribunals named by an Act. It has at least twelve judges, who elect their own President.
Parliament must create courts with High Court status for (a) employment and labour disputes and (b) environment and land disputes. These are the ELRC and the EL

A 1970s US movement: legal decisions are political choices, rules rarely settle cases, and law tends to protect the powerful.

Custom needs two things: states actually behave a certain way (state practice), and they do so because they believe the law requires it (opinio juris).
Long-standing community practices that become binding because people treat them as obligatory.

children.topic: Damage: there must be real loss
children.note: Negligence is not actionable without harm. Typical loss is injury, damage to property, and money lost because of them. Pure money loss on its own is recovered o
General damages cover pain, suffering and loss of amenity. Special damages cover exact money losses, such as hospital bills, and must be specifically proved.

children.topic: Damages: money to make it good
children.note: The usual remedy. Money puts the innocent party where they would have been if the contract had been performed.
The Act makes no difference between sons and daughters, married or unmarried. A custom that excludes daughters cannot override it.
Still in the law, but no execution since 1987. In Mutiso v Republic (2010) the Court of Appeal rejected the mandatory death sentence for murder.
Truth (justification); honest opinion on a matter of public interest; absolute privilege, as for evidence in court or debate in Parliament; and qualified privil
Rules made by a minister or body under power given by an Act: regulations, rules, orders and county by-laws.
Fraud means making a false statement knowingly, without belief in its truth, or recklessly. An honest belief is a defence.
Direct evidence proves a fact straight away (I saw him take the phone). Circumstantial evidence points to it by inference (the phone was found in his bag).

Committing a crime because of threats of death or serious harm. It is very narrow and is generally no defence to murder.
A trustee must act like an ordinary prudent business person managing their own affairs, as Speight v Gaunt (1883) held.
A trustee must not let personal interest clash with duty, and must not make an unauthorised profit from the role.

Actual, open, exclusive and continuous possession, against the owner's rights and without permission, for the whole period.

An unforeseen event, not anyone's fault, makes the contract impossible or pointless. Both sides are released.
The postal rule does not cover instant messages such as telex. Acceptance by instant means counts only when received.
Article 162 requires Parliament to set up a court with High Court status for disputes over the environment and the use, occupation of and title to land.
Everyone is equal before the law. The State must not discriminate on grounds such as sex, race, health, religion or birth, and no more than two-thirds of an ele
Liberal feminists seek real equality; difference feminists want law to recognise real differences; dominance theory (MacKinnon) sees law as male power.

children.topic: Equity will not perfect a gift
children.note: If a gift fails for want of the right steps, equity will not rescue it by calling it a trust. A volunteer (someone who gave nothing) cannot force completion.
In the Earl of Oxford's case, a quarrel between Chancery and the common-law judges was settled for the Crown: where equity and common law conflict, equity preva
The modern English test: the veil may be pierced only where a company is used to dodge a legal duty its controller already had.
The duty to produce enough evidence to make an issue worth considering, for example raising self-defence. It can move between parties.

A rogue who gets goods by fraud has voidable title. If they sell to an honest buyer before the owner cancels the deal, the buyer gets good title.
An executor is named in the will to manage the estate. An administrator is appointed by the court when there is no will or no executor.
A qualified expert (doctor, handwriting examiner, ballistics officer) may give an opinion within their field. The court weighs it and is not bound by it.
Terms starting with F.
What happened between the parties, in a few lines. Keep only the facts the court needed to decide the case.

children.topic: Facts in issue vs relevant facts
children.note: Facts in issue are what the case turns on (was the matatu driver speeding?). Relevant facts help prove them (long skid marks on the road).
Ordinary witnesses say what they saw or heard; drawing conclusions is the court's job.
Ask: but for what the accused did, would the harm have happened? If it would have happened anyway, there is no factual cause.

children.topic: False fact that induced the deal
children.note: There must be a false statement of fact (not opinion or a sales boast) that actually influenced the decision.
Unlawfully restraining someone's freedom to move, even briefly, such as locking a customer in a shop without lawful reason.
Arrangements between spouses or relatives are presumed to be honour-only. The presumption can be rebutted with evidence.
Territory, nationality of the offender, nationality of the victim (passive personality), protection of the state's security, and universal jurisdiction.
The Marriage Act 2014 recognises Christian, civil, customary, Hindu and Islamic marriage. All have the same legal status once valid.
The exact way or extent of the harm need not be foreseen, only its general type, such as physical injury or fire damage.
If directors wrong the company, the company itself is the proper claimant, not individual members. The majority may ratify.

children.topic: Four rights that can never be limited
children.note: Freedom from torture and cruel treatment, freedom from slavery, the right to a fair trial, and the right to habeas corpus.
Montevideo Convention 1933, Article 1: a permanent population, a defined territory, a government, and the capacity to deal with other states.

You may seek, receive and share ideas. It does not cover propaganda for war, incitement to violence, hate speech or advocacy of hatred.
Freehold gives ownership with no end date. You may use, sell, charge or leave the land to heirs, subject to planning and other laws.
Rules should be general, published, not retroactive, clear, not contradictory, fairly stable, possible to obey, and applied as written.

For Christian, civil and Hindu marriages the grounds include adultery, cruelty, desertion, exceptional depravity and irretrievable breakdown. Customary and Isla

The master secondary rule that officials use to identify which rules are valid law.

children.topic: How facts are proved in court
children.note: Evidence is anything that helps a court decide whether a fact is true: what witnesses say, documents and objects.
You pay a deposit, use the goods and pay instalments. Ownership passes at the end, often by a small option-to-buy payment.
A counter-offer kills the original offer. The buyer who offered less could not later accept the first price.

A claimant whose harm flows from their own serious wrongdoing may be refused damages, for example one burglar suing another during a getaway.
The decision-maker got the law wrong: no power at all, used a power for the wrong purpose, or misread the Act.
Covers authorised acts and authorised jobs done in a wrong way, such as a driver speeding on the route.

Good governance, integrity, transparency and accountability, plus sustainable development.
Acting in order to bring about a result. Direct intention is wanting it; indirect intention is seeing it as virtually certain.

A decision so unreasonable that no sensible authority could have made it. The bar is high: disagreeing with the decision is not enough.

The Judicature Act lets Kenyan courts apply the common law, doctrines of equity and old English statutes of general application, as at a fixed date, where Kenya

children.topic: Judicial authority comes from the people
children.note: Courts hold judicial power on behalf of the people and must do justice to all, avoid delay, and focus on substance over technicalities.
Facts so well known that no proof is needed, such as Nairobi being Kenya's capital or which day of the week a date fell on.
Terms starting with K.

children.topic: Land includes what is fixed to it
children.note: In law, land is the ground plus buildings and things firmly attached (fixtures), such as a house or a fence. A parked car is not part of the land.
The main law on registering land and interests, opening land registers and issuing titles. It replaced several older registration laws.
It covers the everyday decisions of ministries, county offices, boards and agencies: licences, permits, dismissals, refunds.

A question that suggests its answer ('You saw him at Gikomba, didn't you?'). Not allowed in chief, allowed in cross.
Leasehold gives exclusive use for a fixed term, usually in return for rent. When it ends, the land goes back to the landlord, often the government or county.
A lease gives exclusive possession for a fixed or periodic term, usually for rent. A mere permission to use land is only a licence.
A man owned nearly all shares and was the company's pilot. He could still be its employee, so his widow got compensation.
The duty to persuade the court on an issue. In criminal cases it rests on the prosecution throughout. See Woolmington v DPP.
If a public body clearly promised something, or always followed a practice, it may not suddenly go back on it unfairly.
Libel is defamation in lasting form, such as print, posts or broadcasts. Slander is passing form, such as spoken words or gestures.
Shareholders lose only what they put in or promised for their shares. The company's creditors cannot chase their personal assets.
A hybrid under Kenya's Limited Liability Partnerships Act: partners run it like a partnership, but the LLP is a legal person and partners' liability is limited.
Give words their plain, ordinary meaning, even if the result is harsh. Respects Parliament but can produce absurd results.

A company should not hand its capital back to members except as the law allows. Dividends come from profits only.
A court can order one spouse to support the other, looking at each person's needs and means. Either husband or wife may be ordered to pay.
An order forcing a public body to do a public duty it is refusing to do, such as issuing a document it must issue.
Goods sold by description must match it. 'Pishori rice' must be pishori. Reliance on the description matters.
